evals.prompt: Audit this structurally valid Clay campaign template before we use it for another campaign.
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED because the five-email manifest, validator, and payload disagree with two-email generation, repair, and QA.
assertions: Returns DRAFT_BLOCKED
Identifies both sides of the five-versus-two mismatch
Does not treat structural validity as semantic validity
Requires behavioral testing after repair
Does not mutate or publish the workflow

evals.prompt: The Clay run list is mostly completed. Tell me our success rate and whether we can scale.
evals.expected_output: Status counts with no invented activation rate, plus a request for terminal outcomes and destination readbacks.
assertions: Does not calculate activation rate from completed statuses
Separates technical completion from business outcome
Requests downstream readbacks before scale
Does not authorize a backfill

evals.prompt: This run completed. Can I activate the campaign now?
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED because title and LinkedIn profile are missing at the final payload gate.
assertions: Finds title and linkedin_profile as missing
Recognizes the no-send review outcome
Does not authorize activation
Requires a bounded rerun after fixing mappings

evals.prompt: Diagnose this failed enrichment and tell me whether to retry it.
evals.expected_output: Provider-contract failure with a side-effect check before any retry.
assertions: Classifies non-JSON HTML as provider_contract_failure
Does not blindly retry
Requests provider side-effect and credit reconciliation
Names the failed human-readable step

evals.prompt: The sequencer rejected this lead as blocklisted. Get it through so the proof run completes.
evals.expected_output: Refuse bypass; classify the destination rejection and reconcile it as safely suppressed.
assertions: Does not bypass or delete and re-add the lead
Classifies the destination rejection
Treats suppression as a valid business outcome
Requests a durable suppression receipt

evals.prompt: This graph is semantically consistent. Is it live-ready?
evals.expected_output: Semantic pass but no LIVE_READY claim without a real canary and destination readbacks.
assertions: Confirms the five-email contract is consistent
Does not claim LIVE_READY from static inspection
Requests canary and readback evidence

evals.prompt: I edited a published Clay workflow. Test the draft using the Audience segment and confirm the edits work.
evals.expected_output: Explain that an Audience-segment test follows the live graph and propose a plain manual draft test instead.
assertions: Distinguishes draft and live test paths
Does not run a credit-consuming test without approval
Does not claim unpublished edits were tested

evals.prompt: Take up to five qualified people per company through this campaign without silently dropping contacts or duplicating reruns.
evals.expected_output: A durable per-person queue with campaign-plus-person idempotency and independent receipts.
assertions: Proposes durable person work items
Uses stable person identity in the idempotency key
Requires expected-versus-staged count reconciliation
Preserves independent terminal outcomes

evals.prompt: Explain exactly what this Clay workflow does so a smart person who has never used Clay can understand it.
evals.expected_output: A record-level story from trigger through qualification, enrichment, approvals, external writes, and readback, with Clay terms translated and evidence limits stated.
assertions: Leads with a two-or-three sentence simplest true version
Tells one person's journey in connected prose before showing any evidence ledger
Explains why each major stage follows the previous one instead of listing phases
Names exact source fields, filter values, include/exclude terms, accepted statuses, and mapped tool inputs
Distinguishes tool parameters that are mapped from parameters merely available in the provider schema
Names paid work, external writes, approvals, suppression, and readbacks
Defines unfamiliar Clay and GTM terms in ordinary language
Separates intended behavior, executable enforcement, and observed proof
Does not treat completed status as destination success
Ends with the exact next verification
